claims.quote: Now she is 31, and her private company in Redmont, called Veridrop, has 500 employees and has raised more than $400 million from equity sales to investors who have valued it at more than $9 billion.
claims.why: Check headcount, capital raised, valuation and location.

claims.quote: It currently offers more than 200–and is ramping up to offer more than 1,000–of the most commonly ordered blood diagnostic tests, all without the need for a syringe.
claims.why: Check the size of the test menu.

claims.quote: The company has performed as many as 70 different tests from a single draw of 25 to 50 microliters collected in a vial the size of a pencil eraser, which Marlowe has named a “microwell.”
claims.why: Check whether so many tests from so small a sample has been validated by anyone independent.

claims.quote: Precisely how Veridrop accomplishes all of this is a trade secret.
claims.why: Check whether secrecy blocks any check of the method.

claims.quote: Marlowe will only say, and this is more than she has said before, that her company uses “the same fundamental chemical methods” as existing labs do.
claims.why: Check whether this explains how small samples give standard results.

claims.quote: The company leases a 262,000-square-foot building at the edge of the Redmont research park, where its laboratory fills the ground floor.
claims.why: Check the lease and floor area.

claims.quote: The laboratory's director says the work is ordinary laboratory work.
Its prices are often a half to a quarter of what independent labs charge, and a quarter to a tenth of what hospital labs bill.
